==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|grade||a grade, degree}}, from {{der|en|la|gradus||a step, pace, degree}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*graðus}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰradʰ-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*gʰredʰ-||to walk, go}}. {{doublet|en|gradus}}.

Cognate with {{cog|got|𐌲𐍂𐌹𐌸𐍃||step, grade}}, {{cog|bar|Gritt||step, stride}}, {{cog|lt|grìdiju||to go, wander}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɡɹeɪd/}}
** {{IPA|en|[ɡɹeɪd]|a=US,RP}}
** {{IPA|en|[ɡɹɛjd]|a=SSB}}
** {{IPA|en|[ɡɹeːd]|a=CA}}
** {{IPA|en|[ɡɹæɪd]|a=AU}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-grade.ogg|a=US}}
* {{homophones|en|grayed|greyed<aa:pane-pain>}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪd|s=1}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[rating]].
#: {{ux|en|This fine-'''grade''' coin from 1837 is worth a good amount.}}
#: {{ux|en|prime '''grade''' beef}}
# {{senseid|en|Q18185}} {{lb|en|chiefly|North America|Philippines}} Performance on a test or other evaluation(s), expressed by a number, letter, or other symbol; a [[score]].
#: {{syn|en|mark}}
#: {{ux|en|He got a good '''grade''' on the test.}}
#: {{ux|en|I gave him a good '''grade''' for effort.}}
#: {{ux|en|You need a '''grade''' of at least 80% in first-year calculus to be admitted to the CS major program.}}
# A [[degree]] or [[level]] of something; a position within a scale; a degree of quality.
#* {{quote-web
|en
|year=1986–2012
|author=paul wheaton permaculture
|title=Diatomaceous Earth (food grade): bug killer you can eat!
|site=richsoil.com
|url=http://www.richsoil.com/diatomaceous-earth.jsp
|accessdate=2014-03-17
|passage=There are a lot of varieties of diatomaceous earth, so when you are shopping, be sure to get the right stuff! Make sure that you get food '''grade''' diatomaceous earth. Some people make 3% of the food they eat be diatomaceous earth.
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260926115537/https://richsoil.com/diatomaceous-earth.jsp
|archivedate=26 September 2026
}}
# {{lb|en|linguistics}} [[degree|Degree]] (any of the three stages (positive, comparative, superlative) in the comparison of an adjective or an adverb).
# {{senseid|en|Q275447}} A [[slope]] (up or down) of a roadway or other passage
#: {{ux|en|The '''grade''' of this hill is more than 5 percent.}}
# {{lb|en|North America|Philippines|education}} A level of primary and secondary education.
#: {{ux|en|Clancy is entering the fifth '''grade''' this year.}}
#: {{ux|en|Clancy starts '''grade''' five this year.}}
# {{lb|en|Canada|education}} A student of a particular grade (used with the grade level).
#: {{ux|en|The '''grade fives''' are on a field trip.}}
# An area that has been flattened by a [[grader]] (construction machine).
# The level of the [[ground]].
#: {{ux|en|This material absorbs moisture and is probably not a good choice for use below '''grade'''.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q208528}} {{lb|en|mathematics}} A [[gradian#English:_Q208528|gradian]].
# {{lb|en|geometry}} In a [[linear]] [[system]] of [[divisor]]s on an ''n''-dimensional [[variety]], the number of free intersection points of ''n'' [[generic]] divisors.
# A harsh scraping or cutting; a grating.
# {{lb|en|systematics}} A [[taxon]] united by a level of morphological or physiological complexity that is not a [[clade]].
# {{lb|en|medicine}} The degree of malignity of a tumor expressed on a scale.
# {{lb|en|Philippines|ophthalmology}} An [[eyeglass]] [[prescription]].

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|chiefly|North America}} To assign [[score]]s to the [[component]]s of an [[academic]] [[test]], or to [[overall]] academic performance.
# To organize in grades.
#: {{usex|en|a '''graded''' reader}}
# To [[flatten]], [[level]], or [[smooth]] a large [[surface]], especially with a [[grader]].
#: ''to '''grade''' land before building on it''
# {{lb|en|sewing}} To [[remove]] or [[trim]] part of a [[seam allowance]] from a finished [[seam]] so as to reduce [[bulk]] and make the finished piece more even when turned right side out.
# {{lb|en|patternmaking}} To [[increase]] or [[decrease]] the [[dimensions]] of a garment pattern from the [[initial]] base size in such a way that the overall [[proportions]] of the [[silhouette]] are maintained across all sizes.
# To apply classifying [[label]]s to data (typically by a [[manual]] rather than automatic process).
#: {{usex|en|Brain scans were '''graded''' on a five-point scale of atrophy.}}
# {{lb|en|linguistics}} To [[describe]], [[modify]] or [[inflect]] so as to [[classify]] as to [[degree]].
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1999
|author=Jon Franco; Alazne Landa; Juan Martín
|title=Grammatical Analyses in Basque and Romance Linguistics: Papers in Honor of Mario Saltarelli
|publisher=John Benjamins Publishing
|isbn=9789027236937
|page=65
|passage=He has rightly observed that while -ísimo superlatives are typically prenominal, adjectives '''graded''' with the intensifier muy "very" are characteristically postnominal.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=2014
|author=Angela Downing
|title=English Grammar: A University Course
|publisher=Routledge
|isbn=9781317610977
|page=430
|passage=Adjectives '''graded''' for comparative and superlative degree can function both attributively and predicatively. Most descriptive adjectives are gradable: As modifiers of a noun ''Have you got a larger size?'' {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2020|title=Prekmurje Slovene Grammar: Avgust Pavel’s Vend nyelvtan (1942)|page=82|publisher=BRILL|isbn=9789004419148
|passage=Similarly to the Hungarian adjectives '''graded''' with the suffix -ik, in place of naj, najto, or, in agreement with the noun, -najte, -najta, -najto forms occur, e.g., najtolepsi or najtelepsi, najtelepsa, najtelepse 'most beautiful'.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[pass]] imperceptibly from one grade into another.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1924|author=w:EM Forster|title=w:A Passage to India|page=34|publisher=Penguin|year_published=2005
|passage=And there were circles even beyond these – […] humanity '''grading''' and drifting beyond the educated vision, until no earthly invitation can embrace it.}}
# {{lb|en|Canada|dated|intransitive}} To [[pass]] from one school grade into the next.
#: {{ux|en|I '''graded''' out of grade two and three and arrived in Miss Hanson's room.}}
